summary: Audited the captured hashicorp/raft snapshot and established that it is byte-identical to the released upstream copy of the same revision (diff -rq vs the local module cache reports no differing file), so this is a genuine-defect hunt rather than a mutation hunt. Found and sourced a concrete context/authority-basis defect in the public configuration API: Raft.GetConfiguration() (api.go:895-903) responds a configurationsFuture built only from the atomic latestConfiguration copy, so ConfigurationFuture.Index() (future.go:267-270) is the constant 0 in every call, even though the main thread holds the real r.configurations.latestIndex and serves it over configurationsCh (raft.go:882-890, the path snapshot.go uses); Stats() republishes that zero as latest_configuration_index (api.go:1183-1189), making it a constant rather than an observation. The consumer duty is documented: AddVoter and friends describe prevIndex as the index of the only configuration the change may apply to, but nextConfiguration only enforces it when prevIndex > 0 (configuration.go:229), so a caller taking the index from the only public source and passing it back silently loses the compare-and-swap protection while the call still succeeds. Recorded three reusable behaviors, one interpretation (explained, defect asserted on source grounds, limitations noted), one key gap, and a second independent investigation with its discriminator on duties lost when authority is lost by Shutdown() rather than step-down (queued apply futures, already noted at raft_test.go:40-42). A discriminating harness (assurance_generated_test.go) samples the public index next to the main-thread latestIndex on one running bootstrapped leader; it is written and validated but not yet executed, so the observed value is still unknown.
